title: R-Type
build: tape version 1, cracked to disk by Oneway (R-TYPE++), level-skip key added

records.c: The ending's copy of the stages' music driver, the same code moved up by $490 bytes (from $6370 to $6800), with the same entry table: $6800 plays one frame (called from the ending's raster interrupt), $6803 silences the SID, $6806 asks for a sound effect, $6809 asks for a tune, $680C points the driver at a block of music data (X low, Y high; the ending passes $71D0).
Entry 2: silence (jumps to music_stop).
Entry 3: ask for a sound effect, A the effect and X the voice (jumps to request_sound).
Entry 4: ask for a tune, A its number (jumps to request_tune).
Entry 5: point the driver at a music data block (jumps to music_data).
The low nibble written to $D418 with the filter mode: the master volume.

The tune's position in its tracks, then the scratch byte $6811, the loop position ($6812), the end position ($6813), the rows in a pattern ($6814), the row count ($6815) and the music-on flag ($6816).

The ending, jumped to by the crackers' loader once it has loaded file Y after stage 8. Interrupts off, the KERNAL banked in ($01 = $36) and the CIA's interrupts stopped; the screen at $CC00 with the character set at $C000 ($D018 = $30, video bank 3 through $DD00), border and background black. Points the music driver at its data ($71D0), starts tune 0 at full volume ($680F = 15), clears the screen to blank characters in white, copies the ending's 64-character font ($8502) to $C000, lays the text out (ending_layout) and sets up the stars (ending_stars_init). Then the raster interrupt on line $FA (ending_irq) takes over.
An entry into ending_start that other code jumps to.
Start the crawl: fine scroll 7, the raster interrupt on line $FA through $0314 = $81C1, the line count ($8250) at 0 and the text pointer ($02/$03) at $B018.
Wait until the text has scrolled $43 lines.
Then fade the music out: each time the line count moves on, the driver's volume ($680F) goes down by one, until it is silent.

When the space bar is pressed (bit 4 of $DC01), copy ending_reset to $0100 and run it, starting the wipe at $0200.

Copied to $0100 and run there when space is pressed after the ending: banks every ROM out ($01 = $34), fills all memory from $0200 to $FFFF with zeros, banks the ROMs back ($01 = $37) and jumps into the KERNAL's reset ($FCE2). The game is wiped and the machine starts again.

Clears the buffer at $B000-$BFFF, then lays the ending text ($8251) into it from $B400 on, one screen line of 40 bytes per text line: a 0 or $0D ends a line, $D3 ends the text, and letters (ASCII $40 and up) become screen codes by taking $40 off.

The raster interrupt: moves the stars every frame and plays the music ($6800). Every third frame ($824F) the screen scrolls up a pixel ($824E into $D011); every eighth step the 25 rows at the text pointer are copied to the screen ($CC00) and, until the line count reaches $4C, the pointer moves on a line ($02/$03 plus 40), so the text crawls up. The line count ($8250) goes up to $C8 and the main loop fades the music by it.
Play the music and return from the interrupt.
Every third frame: the next pixel of the scroll.
A whole line has scrolled: copy 25 lines of the buffer to the screen.
